title: Pride
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Pride is the sinful exaltation of self against God and others. It refuses humble dependence, resists correction, seeks self-glory, and trusts personal wisdom, strength, or righteousness above the Lord.
summary: Pride is the sinful exaltation of self against God and others. It refuses humble dependence, resists correction, seeks self-glory, and trusts personal wisdom, strength, or righteousness above the Lord.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the humble Savior who humbled Himself to the point of death. He saves proud sinners by grace and teaches His people to walk in lowliness, repentance, and dependence on God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Pride places self where God belongs. It may appear as arrogance, self-reliance, entitlement, defensiveness, comparison, contempt, refusal to repent, or confidence in one’s own righteousness.

Scripture warns that pride leads to destruction. God opposes the proud because pride rejects His rightful rule and seeks glory that belongs to Him alone. Pride was at the root of much rebellion and remains deadly to the soul.

Pride can look religious. The Pharisee in Jesus’ parable prayed with confidence in himself and contempt for another. Religious pride is especially dangerous because it can hide behind morality, knowledge, or ministry.

Christ humbles and saves proud sinners. He, though exalted, humbled Himself in obedience. Those who receive Him learn to stop boasting in self and boast only in the Lord.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Pride keeps people from receiving grace because it insists on self-sufficiency. It makes correction feel like attack, repentance feel like weakness, and dependence feel humiliating.

This doctrine is necessary for both the outwardly successful and the deeply broken. Pride can boast in strength or hide in self-protective shame. Christ calls both to humble surrender before God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Humble yourself before God. Confess where you resist correction, seek control, despise others, or trust your own righteousness. Look to the humility of Christ, receive grace, and practice lowly obedience in your speech, service, repentance, and relationships.
